chapter_title: Concerning the Five Saviours, the Resurrectors of Those Who Are Dead, Together with the Five Resurrections
chapter_note: Despite heavy lacunae, the dominant layer is a pentadic, systematic list of “resurrectors” (¶3–6) stated in an impersonal cosmological register. The chapter is wrapped by a brief hagiographic/dialogue incipit (¶1–2) and ends with a beatitude-style exhortation (¶7), which reads as later pastoral/application rather than part of the impersonal degree-teaching.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic incipit (“Once again the enlightener speaks”), typical Kephalaia framing rather than cosmological exposition.
Extremely lacunose continuation immediately after the formulaic opening; lacks any stable cosmological mapping language and most likely belongs to the same editorial frame/delivery context.
Begins the pentadic teaching list (“second resurrector”), a structural/degree marker characteristic of the older systematic substrate even though the content is damaged.

paragraphs.core_text: And the third resurrector is the Father, the First [...], because by his word shall all lives [...] gather in and go to him, and they receive [...] and rest.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological mechanism (“by his word shall all lives gather… receive… rest”) describing what the being does within the system, not applying it to contemporary institutions or audience behavior.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth resurrector is the Light Mind, because [...]. ⟨p.46⟩
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the numbered pentadic sequence with a named cosmological entity (“Light Mind”) in expository form; no citation or pastoral address.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth resurrector to the good [...] is the Father, the First established one [...]. [He ...] all the powers, and he stands firm [...]. He shall unveil the [...] over them [...], and he draws them to him [...], his will [...], and he [...] them, and he stands them up [...] there, and they remain until [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extended impersonal process-description (unveiling, drawing, standing up powers) inside the cosmic system; maintains the systematic list structure rather than shifting to exhortation or institutional identification.
Beatitude/exhortation (“Blessed is every one who…”) shifts from describing cosmic mechanics to blessing/audience-facing moral application; no longer a cosmos→cosmos mapping.
